reference.source: Dhingra, Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat
clinicalPearls: Defined as a rapid-onset sensorineural hearing loss developing over hours to a few days, most often unilateral
It is an otological emergency where prompt evaluation and treatment offer the best chance of hearing recovery
Patients often report a blocked ear, tinnitus and sometimes vertigo, and may notice the loss on waking
Tuning fork tests help confirm a sensorineural pattern: Weber lateralises to the better-hearing ear and Rinne remains positive
The majority of cases are idiopathic, but identifiable causes include infection, vascular events, trauma, ototoxic drugs and, importantly, vestibular schwannoma
Management principles centre on early corticosteroid therapy, given systemically or intratympanically, after excluding a conductive cause
MRI of the internal auditory meatus is important to exclude a retrocochlear lesion such as acoustic neuroma
Delay in diagnosis and treatment reduces the likelihood of hearing recovery, so urgent referral is essential
reference.pathophysiology: Sudden sensorineural hearing loss reflects acute dysfunction of the cochlea or auditory nerve. Although often idiopathic, proposed mechanisms include viral infection or inflammation of the labyrinth, microvascular compromise of the cochlear blood supply, rupture of intracochlear membranes, and autoimmune injury. These processes damage the delicate hair cells and neural elements or disturb the cochlear ionic and metabolic environment, producing abrupt hearing loss. A minority result from identifiable structural causes such as a vestibular schwannoma compressing the cochlear nerve, which is why imaging is required.
additionalDifferentials: Impacted cerumen or other conductive causes (must be excluded)
Central causes such as stroke affecting auditory pathways
additionalInvestigations: Otoscopy and tuning fork tests to distinguish sensorineural from conductive loss
Pure tone audiometry to confirm and quantify the sensorineural loss
MRI of the internal auditory meatus and posterior fossa to exclude retrocochlear pathology
Blood tests for infective, inflammatory or autoimmune causes as indicated
Vestibular assessment when vertigo accompanies the hearing loss
redFlags: Sudden unilateral hearing loss itself, which is an emergency requiring urgent assessment and treatment
Accompanying neurological signs or severe vertigo suggesting a central or serious cause
Progressive or fluctuating loss with tinnitus indicating possible vestibular schwannoma
Bilateral sudden loss suggesting a systemic, autoimmune or ototoxic process
reference.prognosis: Outcome is variable; a substantial proportion recover partially or fully, particularly with early treatment, but severe loss, delayed presentation, vertigo and poor initial audiometry are associated with worse recovery.
pitfalls: Dismissing sudden hearing loss as wax or a benign blocked ear and delaying treatment
Failing to distinguish sensorineural from conductive loss with tuning fork tests
Not arranging MRI to exclude a vestibular schwannoma
Missing the narrow window in which corticosteroid therapy is most effective
references: Dhingra, Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat
management: Commence early systemic corticosteroid therapy once a conductive cause is excluded, as the mainstay to maximise the chance of hearing recovery
Offer intratympanic corticosteroid injection as primary treatment where systemic steroids are contraindicated, or as salvage after an incomplete response
Consider adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy in selected patients presenting early
Withdraw any ototoxic drugs and treat identifiable causes, using antiviral therapy for infection and immunosuppression for suspected autoimmune inner-ear disease
Arrange MRI of the internal auditory meatus to exclude vestibular schwannoma and other retrocochlear pathology
Track recovery with serial pure-tone audiometry and provide vestibular rehabilitation where vertigo is present
Refer to ENT and audiology for hearing rehabilitation with hearing aids or cochlear implantation if loss persists
